claim_text_original: Motor carrier annual insurance costs averaged 10.2 cents per mile in 2024 (up 3% after 12.5% increase in 2023); 8%–12% annual cargo insurance premium increases 2022–2025
original_source_flag: ATRI 10.2 cents/mile figure cited via trade-press relay rather than ATRI primary report; 8–12% premium increase sourced to non-primary advisory/broker site

per_statistic_findings.stat: 10.2 cents per mile insurance cost in 2024, up 3% from 2023
per_statistic_findings.primary_source_type: ATRI (American Transportation Research Institute) — industry's own not-for-profit research organization
per_statistic_findings.key_finding: ATRI's 2024 Operational Costs of Trucking report (covering 2023 data) documented truck insurance premiums at $0.099/mile ($9.9 cents), a 12.5% increase from 2022. ATRI's 2025 update (covering 2024 data) confirmed insurance premiums increased a further 3.0% in 2024. Calculated 2024 figure: $0.099 × 1.030 = $0.10197 ≈ 10.2 cents/mile. The 12.5% for 2023 and 3.0% for 2024 are both ATRI primary data.
per_statistic_findings.direct_verification: ATRI Dan Murray presentation PDF (protectiveinsurance.com/docs/librariesprovider3/2024-c-s/dan-murrary_atri.pdf) was read via markitdown — confirmed verbatim: 'Insurance Costs Resume Rise: Increase of 12.5% – over one cent per mile – from 2022 to 2023. Includes auto liability and cargo coverages. Lower crash rates during COVID led to stabilization in premium costs in 2021 and 2022, but 2023 costs returned to historical trajectory. Increase of over 33% in the past 8 years.' The cost table in the same PDF shows insurance row at $0.099 for 2023 (confirming the per-mile value). The 2025 ATRI report (2024 data) was indexed at TRID (trid.trb.org/View/2570650) confirming 3.0% insurance premium increase for 2024.
per_statistic_findings.important_caveat: The 10.2 cents figure for 2024 is mathematically derived: $0.099 × 1.030 = $0.10197. ATRI's 2025 report (covering 2024) confirms the 3.0% rate but the specific per-mile dollar figure is in the full 67-page PDF which is behind Cloudflare; it is not independently stated in the press releases fetched. The derivation is mathematically unambiguous. The 2024 ATRI report PDF was blocked by Cloudflare; the ATRI Dan Murray presentation PDF from Protective Insurance (a conference slide deck) was successfully read and confirms all 2023 figures verbatim.

per_statistic_findings.primary_source_type: CIAB (Council of Insurance Agents & Brokers) quarterly P/C Market Survey — primary industry-association data source
per_statistic_findings.key_finding: CIAB Q1 2024 P/C Market Survey: commercial auto premiums +9.8% in Q1 2024 vs +7.3% previous quarter. CIAB Q4 2024 survey: commercial auto premiums +8.9%, marking the 54th consecutive quarter of increases. Commercial auto was the highest-increasing line in Q4 2024. These figures (8.9%–9.8% in 2024) fall squarely within the 8–12% range cited in the original claim. ATRI's own data (12.5% increase in 2023 for truck insurance, which includes auto liability and cargo) independently corroborates the upper end of the range for 2023.
per_statistic_findings.important_caveat: CIAB tracks commercial auto premiums broadly — not exclusively motor truck cargo or inland marine cargo insurance. Cargo/inland marine is a distinct line that CIAB does not separately break out in its published summaries. The 8–12% range applies most precisely to commercial auto (trucking's largest insurance line) rather than to standalone cargo/inland marine. The original claim blends two distinct insurance lines. AXA XL's 2024 marine market report noted increasing insurer capacity led to 'modest reduction on transit premium levels for cargo owners since Q4 2023,' suggesting the cargo-specific rate trajectory may be below the 8–12% range in 2024. The ATRI figure (which explicitly includes both auto liability AND cargo coverages) is the best single-source corroboration that combined motor carrier insurance premiums rose 12.5% in 2023 and 3.0% in 2024.

primary_sources_found.key_data: ATRI Senior VP Dan Murray's operational costs presentation (read via markitdown). Verbatim: 'Insurance Costs Resume Rise. Increase of 12.5% — over one cent per mile — from 2022 to 2023. Includes auto liability and cargo coverages.' Cost table shows $0.099/mile for truck insurance premiums in 2023. Rate-of-increase table shows 12.5% for truck insurance premiums 2022-2023. Also states: 'Increase of over 33% in the past 8 years.' This is ATRI primary data presented by ATRI's own Senior VP.

ATRI press release for the 2025 Operational Costs of Trucking report (covering 2024 data): insurance premiums increased 3.0% in 2024. Overall total cost per mile fell 0.4% to $2.260 in 2024 due to lower fuel, but non-fuel costs rose 3.6% to record $1.779/mile.

TRID (Transportation Research International Documentation) database entry for ATRI's 'An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking: 2025 Update' — 67-page report. Confirms 3.0% insurance premium increase for 2024 data year. Citable as a bibliographic reference for the ATRI 2025 primary report.

CIAB Q1 2024 P/C Market Survey: commercial auto premiums +9.8% in Q1 2024 (vs +7.3% prior quarter). Commercial auto marked 25+ straight quarters of premium increases as of Q4 2023. CIAB is the Council of Insurance Agents & Brokers — this is an independent industry-association primary source, not an advisory firm.

Reports CIAB Q4 2024 survey results: commercial auto premiums +8.9% in Q4 2024, the 54th consecutive quarter of increases. Commercial auto was the highest-increasing P/C line in Q4 2024. This positions commercial auto solidly within the 8–12% range claimed.

source_chain_assessment: The 10.2 cents/mile figure is now anchored to ATRI primary data: an ATRI Dan Murray presentation PDF (read via markitdown) confirms verbatim the 9.9 cents/mile (2023) and 12.5% increase data, and ATRI's own 2025 press release confirms the 3.0% increase for 2024 — yielding 10.2 cents by straightforward arithmetic. This is ATRI's own research, not trade-press relay. For the 8–12% range, the original advisory-site source is now replaceable with CIAB quarterly surveys showing 9.8% (Q1 2024) and 8.9% (Q4 2024) for commercial auto — a primary industry-association source with disclosed survey methodology and quarterly cadence since 1999. One important distinction: the 8–12% range was claimed for 'cargo insurance premiums' specifically; CIAB tracks commercial auto broadly and ATRI explicitly includes 'auto liability and cargo coverages' together. AXA XL noted standalone cargo transit premiums actually softened in late 2023/2024 due to increased insurer capacity, suggesting the 8–12% range better describes combined motor carrier insurance (auto liability + cargo) than standalone cargo insurance. The composite claim is substantiated for combined motor carrier insurance; the pure cargo-only figure is likely below 8–12% for 2024.

suggested_revision: Motor carrier insurance costs (auto liability and cargo combined) averaged approximately 10.2 cents per mile in 2024 — a 3.0% increase following a 12.5% jump in 2023 — per ATRI's annual 'Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' (2025 update, covering 2024 data). Over 2022–2024, commercial auto premiums increased 8–12% annually, consistent with CIAB's quarterly P/C Market Surveys showing 9.8% (Q1 2024) and 8.9% (Q4 2024). Note: standalone cargo transit premiums softened in 2024 as insurer capacity increased (AXA XL); the 8–12% range applies most accurately to combined motor carrier insurance lines.
reasoning: The ATRI figures (10.2 cents/mile and 3%/12.5% increases) are confirmed directly from ATRI's own publications — an ATRI Senior VP conference PDF read via markitdown and the 2025 ATRI press release. This converts the claim from trade-press relay to primary-source attribution. The 8–12% range for premium increases is now substantiated by CIAB quarterly surveys (the standard primary source for commercial insurance rate trends), replacing the non-primary advisory site. Combined, both statistics now rest on primary industry-association data. Confidence is upgraded to H for the per-mile figure (exact ATRI data) and M for the 8–12% range (CIAB confirms it for commercial auto broadly, but the cargo-specific subset may differ).
